issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: HAL_RCC_OscConfig(), incorrect flash latency when changing MSI frequency used as SYSCLK
Context: repo=stm32u5xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=USB, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=32
Root cause: Hello @homer242, Thank you for your report.
Fix: Hello, In the current implementation of HAL_RCC_OscConfig(), there is a check to update the flash latency before or after changing the MSI frequency when it is used as SYSCLK.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, USB, bug_report, high, bug, invalid, rcc, HAL_RCC_OscConfig, MSI, SYSCLK, STM32U5A5, NMI

Technical details:
Hello, In the current implementation of HAL_RCC_OscConfig(), there is a check to update the flash latency before or after changing the MSI frequency when it is used as SYSCLK. However, the implemented logic is reversed: increasing the MSI clock range actually decreases its frequency. As a result, the flash latency is not updated in the correct order. I was able to reproduce the problem on a board based on STM32U5A5. An NMI exception is triggered (caused by a FLASH ECC error) when MSI is used as SYSCLK and its frequency is changed from 48 MHz to 12 MHz. I fixed the issue locally by reversing the order between the flash latency update and the MSI frequency change in HAL_RCC_OscConfig(). I could share this patch if needed.

Problem: HAL_RTCEx_BKUPErase and HAL_RTCEx_BKUPBlock_Enable erroneously use "WRITE_REG" instead of "WRITE_BIT"
Context: repo=stm32u5xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=26
Root cause: Hi @sk-waymont, Looks like you're right.
Fix: In file stm32u5xx_hal_rtc_ex.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, rtc, HAL_RTCEx_BKUPErase, HAL_RTCEx_BKUPBlock_Enable, WRITE_REG, WRITE_BIT, TAMP, CR2

Technical details:
In file stm32u5xx_hal_rtc_ex.c, functions HAL_RTCEx_BKUPErase and HAL_RTCEx_BKUPBlock_Enable use the WRITE_REG macro instead of WRITE_BIT. This results in the entire TAMP->CR2 register being reset, which I do not believe is an intended side-effect of these functions. void HAL_RTCEx_BKUPErase(RTC_HandleTypeDef *hrtc) { UNUSED(hrtc); WRITE_REG(TAMP->CR2, TAMP_CR2_BKERASE); } void HAL_RTCEx_BKUPBlock_Enable(RTC_HandleTypeDef *hrtc) { UNUSED(hrtc); WRITE_REG(TAMP->CR2, TAMP_CR2_BKBLOCK); } Suggestion is to change these WRITE_REG to SET_BIT as below: void HAL_RTCEx_BKUPErase(RTC_HandleTypeDef *hrtc) { UNUSED(hrtc); SET_BIT(TAMP->CR2, TAMP_CR2_BKERASE); } void HAL_RTCEx_BKUPBlock_Enable(RTC_HandleTypeDef *hrtc) { UNUSED(hrtc); SET_BIT(TAMP->CR2, TAMP_CR2_BKBLOCK); }

Key comments:
Hi @sk-waymont, Looks like you're right. Thank you for this heads-up. the WRITE_REG() is defined at the [CMSIS](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis-device-u5/blob/6e67187dec98035893692ab2923914cb5f4e0117/Include/stm32u5xx.h#L181) level as shown below: c #define WRITE_REG(REG, VAL) ((REG) = (VAL)) Instead, it should be replaced by the SET_BIT() macro defined as below: c #define SET_BIT(REG, BIT) ((REG) |= (BIT)) Let's have this fixed. I'll log an internal tracker. See also #25 ST Internal Reference: 217271 Fixed in Commit: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32u5xx-hal-driver/commit/8663a8b195ee416d7eedd088cdc5890ded38ae04

issues.issue_title: HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady() NACK Bug
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady() NACK Bug
Context: repo=stm32u5xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=15
Root cause: Hello @bencowperthwaite, Thank you for the report.
Fix: Changes introduced in V1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, bug_report, high, bug, spotted before customer, i2c, HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady, HAL_ERROR, START, NACK, STOPF, NACKF

Technical details:
Changes introduced in V1.5 of stm32u5xx_hal_i2c.c now mean that HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady() will always return a HAL_ERROR immediately if a slave NACKs, without any repeated trials or a timeout. After the START is generated (line #3480), a subsequent NACK will cause execution to drop out of the while loop and the intention is then to wait until the STOPF flag is reset (line #3535). Due to the if statement at #3513 we know that the NACK flag is definitely set when entering I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout(). A change to I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout for v1.5 at line #7292 now means that I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout() will call **I2C_IsErrorOccurred(), which returns HAL_ERROR if the NACK Flag is set**. We already know that the NACKF flag is set, that's why we've called I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout(). The above causes I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout() to return HAL_ERROR, which is treated as fatal at line #3535 which returns HAL_ERROR immediately without re-trying. I don't think this is intended behaviour, as calling a function which return HAL_ERROR on a NACKF **because you've detected a NACKF** is pointless. Also, it is normal for NACKs to be used by I2C devices to signal that they are busy as part of an ACK polling regime. See https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/devicedoc/21713m.pdf for one such example, where ACK polling is expected following a write to detect the end of EEPROM activity before the next transaction. We're currently stuck in limbo between HAL versions, as V1.6 fixes some other bugs whilst introducing this one. Can you confirm that it is safe to selectively downgrade stm32u5xx_hal_i2c.c and stm32u5xx_hal_i2c.h to v1.4 whilst upgrading the rest of HAL? I assume the API presented by stm32u5xx_hal_i2c.h is intended to be unchanged across HAL revisions? Otherwise can you advise a fix?

ST Internal Reference: 191244 Hi @manisht-mwp, According to our development teams, this is coded this way on purpose. Indeed, as you can see from [RM0456](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0456-stm32u5-series-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf), revision 5, there are two cryptographic instances: AES (chapter 49) and SAES (chapter 50). Keywords: HAL, bug_report, high, bug, spotted before customer, RTOS, STM32U545, HAL_SRAM_MODULE_ENABLED, HAL_NAND_MODULE_ENABLED, HAL_NOR_MODULE_ENABLED

Technical details:
In trying to get Zephyr RTOS working on the Nucleo U545RE-Q board, I discovered header inclusion issues building the HAL for the STM32U545 SoC. Zephyr RTOS makes use of the "stm32u5xx_hal_driver" for some interactions with the ST hardware, and builds the HAL by copying the default "stm32_hal_conf_template.h" to "stm32_hal_conf.h", leaving all options enabled. However, some of the modules (specifically HAL_SRAM_MODULE_ENABLED, HAL_NAND_MODULE_ENABLED and HAL_NOR_MODULE_ENABLED) do not compile for the STM32U545. Based on recommendations from a engineer in the Zephyr forums, I modeled changes to four files ((stm32u5xx_hal_sram.h, stm32u5xx_hal_nor.h, stm32u5xx_hal_nand.h and stm32u5xx_ll_fmc.h) with appropriate "#ifdef" checks using the example for the "stm32g4xx_hal_driver", and this allows the code to build for the U545 series. Clearly, I'd appreciate ST (and others) review of these changes to ensure correctness. I'll submit a PR shortly so the changes can be reviewed.

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * custom board * OZone **Describe the bug (skip if none)** I am interfacing a SPI graphics controller on STM32U585 and to update the frame buffer data, I have to send a single byte of command followed by n bytes as RGB data(more than 65532 bytes), however between I have to toggle a GPIO in between, which controls command/data mode. To accomplish this, I am sending the single command byte by using **HAL_SPI_Transmit_IT**, and eventually I will toggle the GPIO and initiate the TX DMA transmission for RGB data on HAL_SPI_TxCpltCallback and by using **HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA**(multiple iterations as the whole data is more than 65532 bytes which exceed the single shot of DMA). Crash happens in the following line **as hspi->hdmarx is null** in time of comparison due to not using RX DMA. [if (HAL_IS_BIT_CLR(cfg1, SPI_CFG1_TXDMAEN | SPI_CFG1_RXDMAEN) || ((hspi->hdmarx) && (State != HAL_SPI_STATE_BUSY_RX) && (hspi->hdmarx->Mode != DMA_LINKEDLIST_CIRCULAR)) || ((hspi->hdmatx) && (State != HAL_SPI_STATE_BUSY_TX) && (hspi->hdmatx->Mode != DMA_LINKEDLIST_CIRCULAR)))](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32u5xx_hal_driver/blob/6a00c6e1cc756c9804b3044dcd4238f5612adff0/Src/stm32u5xx_hal_spi.c#L2930) **Additional context** I have changed that comparison line as follow: /* DMA Normal Mode */ if (HAL_IS_BIT_CLR(cfg1, SPI_CFG1_TXDMAEN | SPI_CFG1_RXDMAEN) || ((hspi->hdmarx) && (State != HAL_SPI_STATE_BUSY_RX) && (hspi->hdmarx->Mode != DMA_LINKEDLIST_CIRCULAR)) || ((hspi->hdmatx) && (State != HAL_SPI_STATE_BUSY_TX) && (hspi->hdmatx->Mode != DMA_LINKEDLIST_CIRCULAR))) but another issue I am facing now is that actually my DMA transmission will only work once and would fail in the second iteration as SPI state is not equal to HAL_SPI_STATE_READY in time of calling HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA in HAL_SPI_TxCpltCallback. It seems that SPI state would not be resetted in the second call of HAL_SPI_TxCpltCallback which would happen the after completion of first DMA transmission. Apparently, the following line of code would not get called at all to close the transfer: [SPI_CloseTransfer](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32u5xx_hal_driver/blob/6a00c6e1cc756c9804b3044dcd4238f5612adff0/Src/stm32u5xx_hal_spi.c#L2968) Actually after completion of first DMA transfer, SPI_CFG1_TXDMAEN is 1 so the comparison would fail and the aforementioned line would not get called. I wonder if this is an edge case flaw? Or if I am not able to perform the **next DMA transfer in HAL_SPI_TxCpltCallback** at all?

Key comments:
Hi @ramin-raeisi, Regarding the first issue you have reported it has been already spotted and fixed internally. The fix will be made available in the frame of a future release. Concerning the second issue, the SPI state is updated to HAL_SPI_STATE_READY just after closing the transfer and clearing flags. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32u5xx_hal_driver/blob/6a00c6e1cc756c9804b3044dcd4238f5612adff0/Src/stm32u5xx_hal_spi.c#L2970 Thus, when calling HAL_SPI_TxCpltCallback() the SPI state is already set to **HAL_SPI_STATE_READY**.
